skill.displayName: Price Monitor & Daily Excel Report Bot

llm.summary: The skill behaves like a price-scraper/emailer as described, but there are mismatches and missing declarations (notably SMTP environment variables and browser/driver requirements), so its requirements and runtime needs are incoherent and warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the code: it scrapes product pages, builds Excel reports, and emails them. However the registry metadata claims no required env vars or binaries, while SKILL.md and scripts/run.py clearly expect SMTP credentials and Selenium/Chrome (chromedriver + browser). The skill will also write scraped data to data/raw and data/reports. These undeclared runtime requirements are inconsistent with the registry.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the script stick to the stated purpose (scrape URLs from config/urls.txt, save raw data, create a report, email it). But SKILL.md instructs storing SMTP secrets in OpenClaw and the runtime reads them from environment variables even though the registry lists none — the instructions thus depend on secrets not declared in the skill manifest. The instructions and code also require and instantiate a Chrome webdriver (Selenium) which implies access to local browser binaries and drivers not mentioned in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with an included Python script (no install spec). That reduces supply-chain risk, but the skill requires external system components (Selenium, Chrome/Chromedriver) and Python packages; there are no install steps provided to obtain a browser or driver. The absence of install guidance may cause runtime failures or lead users to install platform components manually.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code expects SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, and REPORT_RECIPIENT (documented in SKILL.md) but the registry lists no required env vars. Requesting SMTP credentials is reasonable for emailing reports, but the omission from the manifest is misleading. Supplying SMTP_USER/PASS grants the skill the ability to send arbitrary emails using those credentials — that is a sensitive capability and should be explicitly declared and limited (use app-specific passwords, verify recipients).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings, and stores only its own data under data/*. No elevated persistence is requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's behavior (scraping pages, saving CSV/XLSX, emailing reports) matches its description, but the manifest is incomplete: it fails to declare the SMTP environment variables and the browser/driver dependencies required at runtime. Before installing: 1) Review the code yourself (or have someone you trust do so); 2) Ensure you have Chrome and a matching chromedriver and the Python packages installed in a contained environment; 3) Only provide an SMTP account with an app-specific password or a throwaway account — do not reuse a primary mailbox credential; 4) Confirm REPORT_RECIPIENT and any scheduled behavior are correct (the skill can send emails to arbitrary addresses if misconfigured); 5) Consider running it in an isolated container/VM to limit data exposure; and 6) Verify scraping complies with target sites' terms and rate limits. If you want to proceed, ask the maintainer (or update the registry) to explicitly declare required env vars and installation steps so the runtime requirements are clear.
